relevant_rejection.annotation_only_reading: If the colors are known to be external comparison annotations and excluded from paper content, a careful human can reject D and uniquely select E by the proof above.
relevant_rejection.reasonable_material_color_reading: The question asks what picture results when the two shown physical papers are placed on a black circle. Red and blue lie exactly on the boundary of the gray source paper, and green on the white source paper. They look like colored edging/ink attached to the shown pieces, with matching edging only in D. No text or visible separate annotation convention states that these particular moving-paper features vanish or may be discarded.
explicit_incompatibility: The source red 0..90 arc and blue 90..180 arc share the same top endpoint and form one continuous semicircular outer arc. Any single rigid movement, including a planar reflection, preserves their endpoint incidence and adjacency.

D red is 0..90 and blue is 180..270. These arcs are separated around the outer circle by a white quadrant and a black quadrant; they do not share an endpoint. Their closest endpoints are sqrt(2) radii apart. They cannot both be the moved edging of one intact source gray semicircle.

E is the only possible uncolored arrangement, but E has no red, blue or green outer-edge ink. In this actual E arrangement both source curved edges lie on the outside of the disk and remain exposed; no overlap is available to hide them.
A/B/C already fail the underlying paper geometry and also lack the edging. Thus the exact color-preserving reading has no matching choice, whereas the annotation-only reading has E.
relevant_rejection.why_not_a_blanket_color_ban: Authorized color styling is not automatically promoted to a new numerical or geometric given. The objection here comes from the task-specific physical transformation of the very objects carrying the colored boundaries and the explicit absence of a matching transformed picture. A purely relational geometry highlight need not have this problem.
relevant_rejection.primary_semantics_claim_disposition: The design statement that colors are annotations and not extra physical ink constraints is an author intention outside the actual question/PNG delivered to the solver. It does not resolve the competing reasonable human reading.
relevant_rejection.no_new_cut_claim: There is no new radius, interior cut, closed source subregion or extra gray paper in this new design. Color transitions at the existing arc midpoint do not draw a cut. That passes the Plane233-specific partition objection but does not settle the different paper-ink issue.
relevant_rejection.basis: Actual image and complete wording plus the explicit adjacency/color-preservation calculation; not the model narratives and not a numerical cap on marks.
